doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Dallas childhood, training and early playing
title: Territory bands and Miles Davis asking about J.K. Miller
summary: Walton explains territory bands and tells how at Cafe Bohemia he met Red Garland and Miles Davis, who asked if he knew Walton's high school band director, a former territory musician.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: You mentioned territory bands. Was that a, a …

That's a term I hear people like Jimmy Heath talkin' about, at that time, and it just happened to be in the Southwest, you know – uh, bands uh, with, uh, black personnel going around playing and uh, uh, Fathead was explainin', uh, gave me a possible explanation for uh …. Oh yeah, how uh, uh, Miles Davis …. When I met him uh, when I, uh … I., I digress again. When I went into the Café Bohemia and I stayed, my family stayed about one block away from the Red Garland family. I mean, his father was still in Dallas, and I'd heard all about it and so I introduced myself to Red Garland. He was standin' next to Miles Davis at the bar, and uh, it was an instant. Red was a guy would say, "Oh, oh, hey my man!" You know, he was an instant friend, you know, [laughs] as compared to Miles was a little standoffish. One reason is because he had a voice impediment. He couldn't … You must have heard recordings of his voice. It was kinda hoarse. So I think he resisted uh conversations because of that. But he uh, when he found out I was from Dallas, he asked me did I know J.K. Miller, which was this guy who teach… our high school band director. So imagine my uh, um, enthusiasm, as it comes to mind, uh, uh, at hearing the great Miles Davis talking about my high school band director. I said, "This must be Heaven," I said to myself about New York then. So uh …
Miles had heard of him as, by virtue of the fact that he had traveled with the territory band.

Yeah, that [inaudible] David Newman's. Yeah, David Newman, when David Newman told me that, I said, "David, I didn't think Miles could have possibly known J.K. Miller 'cause me and David played for J.K." He said, "Well, you know a territory man used to come through there, including St. Louis, East St. Louis, wherever Miles was in it." So I wouldn't be … Miles was in love with trumpet as you know, so he had probably heard him. And he was pretty good for Miles to remember him. So um, I'll always remember that moment.
